strings.d1.s0.name: Petronas Twin Towers Skybridge
strings.d1.s0.tips: Skybridge on level 41 plus the level 86 observation deck (~98 MYR). Tickets sell out online days ahead, so book the first morning slot.
strings.d1.s1.name: KLCC Park
strings.d1.s1.tips: Parkland and fountains at the foot of the towers. This is the spot for your photos of them.
strings.d1.s2.name: Nasi Lemak Wanjo Kampung Baru
strings.d1.s2.tips: A Kampung Baru nasi lemak classic with sambal and chicken, within walking distance of KLCC.
strings.d1.s3.name: Kampung Baru
strings.d1.s3.tips: A Malay village in the middle of the skyscrapers, with wooden houses and street stalls.
strings.d1.s4.name: KL Tower Sky Deck
strings.d1.s4.tips: The glass box at Menara KL and the sunset. It's the best place to see the Petronas Towers from across the city.
strings.d1.b0.name: Suria KLCC Signatures Food Court
strings.d1.b0.tips: Mall food court with laksa and satay.
strings.d1.b1.name: Aquaria KLCC
strings.d1.b1.tips: An aquarium beneath the convention centre. A good rainy-day option.
strings.d2.s0.name: Batu Caves
strings.d2.s0.tips: 30 minutes by KTM train. Climb 272 colourful steps to the giant Murugan statue, and watch out for the monkeys. The morning is cool and quiet.
strings.d2.s1.name: Petaling Street
strings.d2.s1.tips: Chinatown market with fake designer bags and street food. Haggle.
strings.d2.s2.name: Hong Kee Claypot Chicken Rice
strings.d2.s2.tips: Claypot rice cooked over charcoal on Petaling Street. Expect a lunchtime queue.
strings.d2.s3.name: Sri Mahamariamman Temple
strings.d2.s3.tips: KL's oldest Hindu temple, with a colourful gopuram (gateway tower).
strings.d2.s4.name: Central Market Kuala Lumpur
strings.d2.s4.tips: An art deco market with batik and handicrafts, and it's air-conditioned.
strings.d2.b0.name: Kim Lian Kee Hokkien Mee
strings.d2.b0.tips: Hokkien mee since 1927, on Petaling Street.
strings.d2.b1.name: Guan Di Temple
strings.d3.s0.name: Merdeka Square
strings.d3.s0.tips: Independence Square and the Sultan Abdul Samad Building, best in the morning light.
strings.d3.s1.name: Masjid Jamek
strings.d3.s1.tips: A Moorish-style mosque where two rivers meet. Outside visiting hours, admire it from the outside.
strings.d3.s2.name: River of Life Walk
strings.d3.s2.tips: A restored riverside walkway along the Klang River, with blue-lit fountains.
strings.d3.s3.name: Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia
strings.d3.s3.tips: Asia's best Islamic art museum, air-conditioned, with domes and calligraphy.
strings.d3.s4.name: Jalan Alor
strings.d3.s4.tips: Bukit Bintang's street food strip: grilled seafood, satay and char kway teow. It comes alive in the evening.
strings.d3.b0.name: Pavilion KL Food Court
strings.d3.b0.tips: Food court in the Bukit Bintang mall. A good rainy-day option.
strings.d3.b1.name: Perdana Botanical Garden
strings.d3.b1.tips: The city's botanical park, with an orchid garden. An alternative to the museum.
strings.d4.s0.name: Brickfields Little India
strings.d4.s0.tips: A colourful Indian neighbourhood with temples and flower garlands.
strings.d4.s1.name: Thean Hou Temple
strings.d4.s1.tips: A six-tier Chinese temple on a hilltop, with red lanterns and city views.
strings.d4.s2.name: Vishal Food & Catering Brickfields
strings.d4.s2.tips: South Indian food served on a banana leaf. Eat with your hands.
strings.d4.s3.name: Bangsar Village
strings.d4.s3.tips: A stylish neighbourhood with cafes and boutiques.
strings.d4.s4.name: Bangsar Devi's Corner
strings.d4.s4.tips: Roti canai and teh tarik (pulled milk tea) at a 24-hour mamak.
strings.d4.b0.name: Thean Hou Vegetarian Canteen
strings.d4.b1.name: National Museum
strings.d4.b1.tips: The national museum, covering Malaysian history. Good in the rain.
strings.d5.s0.name: Dutch Square Melaka
strings.d5.s0.tips: 2 hours from KL by bus (~15 MYR). See the red Stadthuys and Christ Church, a UNESCO site.
strings.d5.s1.name: A Famosa
strings.d5.s1.tips: The Portuguese fortress gate and St. Paul's Hill, with views over the Strait of Malacca.
strings.d5.s2.name: Jonker Street
strings.d5.s2.tips: Peranakan antique shops and cafes, plus a night market at weekends.
strings.d5.s3.name: Hoe Kee Chicken Rice Ball
strings.d5.s3.tips: Melaka's chicken rice with rice shaped into balls. The queue moves fast.
strings.d5.s4.name: Baba & Nyonya Heritage Museum
strings.d5.s4.tips: A Peranakan townhouse, visited on a guided tour.
strings.d5.b0.name: Nancy's Kitchen Melaka
strings.d5.b0.tips: Nyonya cooking, including ayam pongteh (chicken and potato stew).
strings.d5.b1.name: Melaka River Cruise
strings.d5.b1.tips: A river boat ride. An alternative to the museum.
strings.d6.s0.name: Kuala Selangor Sky Mirror
strings.d6.s0.tips: A mirror-like sandbar that appears at low tide (depends on the lunar calendar, tour ~120 MYR). Malaysia's Uyuni.
strings.d6.s1.name: Kuala Selangor Seafood Restaurant
strings.d6.s2.name: Bukit Melawati
strings.d6.s2.tips: Hilltop fort ruins and silvered leaf monkeys.
strings.d6.s3.name: Kuala Selangor Fireflies Tour
strings.d6.s3.tips: A boat trip through the mangroves at Kampung Kuantan. Watch the fireflies in the dark.
strings.d6.b0.name: Genting Premium Outlets Food Court
strings.d6.b1.name: Sekinchan Rice Fields
strings.d6.b1.tips: Rice fields near Kuala Selangor, best in harvest season.
strings.d7.theme: Temple morning and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Masjid Negara
strings.d7.s0.tips: The National Mosque, with a blue star-shaped dome. Robes are provided during visiting hours.
strings.d7.s1.name: Kuala Lumpur Railway Station
strings.d7.s1.tips: A historic Moorish-style station. Good for photos.
strings.d7.s2.name: Restoran Yut Kee
strings.d7.s2.tips: Hainanese coffee and roti babi since 1928. A fitting farewell lunch.
strings.d7.s3.name: KL Sentral
strings.d7.s3.tips: The KLIA Ekspres takes 28 minutes. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Restoran Nasi Kandar Pelita
strings.d7.b1.name: KL Bird Park
strings.d7.b1.tips: The world's largest free-flight walk-in aviary. An alternative to the mosque.
strings.note0: Use a Touch 'n Go card for the LRT and MRT. Grab taxis are cheap (5-15 MYR within the city). The KLIA Ekspres takes 28 minutes and costs 55 MYR.
strings.note1: November to March is monsoon season: short, heavy downpours, so bring an umbrella. Temperatures stay around 30°C all year.
strings.note2: Malaysian food draws on three cultures: nasi lemak (Malay), char kway teow (Chinese) and roti canai (Indian). Mamak restaurants are open 24 hours.
strings.note3: Shoulders and knees must be covered in mosques and Hindu temples. At Batu Caves, monkeys snatch bags.
strings.note4: Petronas Skybridge tickets sell out days ahead. KL Tower is an alternative with a better view.
strings.note5: Alcohol is expensive because of taxes. Tipping is not expected, and a 10% service charge is added.
strings.transit.name: Touch 'n Go Card
strings.transit.why_chosen: Works on the LRT, MRT, monorail and buses. The KLIA Ekspres is separate.
